en: Record of the Discernment of Falsities,
Volume One. Compiled by Imperial Decree by the Śramaṇa Xiangmai of Yunfeng Chan Monastery on Mount Yuandao.
I have heard that when the Dharma-King governs the world, he propagates the Right Path to save his age;
when the Enlightened Sovereign presides over the court, he expounds the Imperial Ultimate to rescue all beings.
He excises the heterodox and upholds the orthodox, exalts virtue, and distinguishes the deluded from the wise.
Thus, when Yao executed the four wicked ones, the Way flourished throughout the eight quarters;
when the Buddha subdued the six groups of unruly monks, the five regions of India turned their hearts toward him.
These were all for this purpose.
He brings order to chaos, rescues those from the conflagration, and opens the eyes and ears of the world.
Indeed, our Buddha achieved his merit through kalpas past and descended as a spiritual manifestation for the sake of all beings.
Manifesting birth from non-arising;
appearing within the great trichiliocosm for the benefit of beings.
Severing all marks while manifesting marks.
Instantly transforming ten billion lands,
like the bright moon flowing through the sky, universally responding in a thousand rivers;
like the sighing of a long wind, causing the myriad pipes to resonate with sound.
He entices the deluded sons toward the vehicle of the single ultimate,
leads those lost on the path onto the road of the Eightfold Right Path,
and uproots the feverish afflictions of the five turbidities.
They dismantle the cage of the four inversions,
point to the bright pearl beneath one's robes,
and unseal the sutra scrolls within the dust.
He defeated the armies of Māra beneath the Bodhi tree without descending to the imperial court;
he crushed the heretics at the Golden River.
His military prowess subdues all without exception;
his benevolence flows to the ten thousand nations,
and his grace extends to the four modes of birth.
The clouds of compassion shade the heavens up to the Akaniṣṭha realm;
the rain of Dharma moistens boundless realms.
When sentient beings have no response, the Great Sage returns to the Truth.
When the sagely sages succeeded one another in radiating brilliance and maintained the profound paradigm,
there were Aśvaghoṣa and Nāgārjuna who expanded the net of the teaching in Western Heaven,
and Āryadeva and Vasubandhu who erected the banner of the Dharma in Southern India.
Vasubandhu excelled in the virtue of posthumously chastising the corpse;
Dignāga displayed the marvel of the roaring boulder.
In a single moment, they both humbled the non-Buddhist heretics.
His virtuous reputation has been spread throughout the ten thousand ages.
Reaching down to the time when the Golden Countenance was dreamed of in the East and the Jade Horse arrived from the West,
Kāśyapa Mātanga manifested the True Dharma in Luoyang.
The Daoist scriptures were all consumed by fire.
Sengrong defeated the heterodox in Guannei,
leaving the Brahman speechless and unable to utter a word.
He suspended the sun of the Buddha over the dark alleys of the world and fanned the breeze of compassion across the realm;
eminent talents followed one another in succession, and men of outstanding virtue joined in a fragrant lineage.
Thus, the Dharma Master Qifa of the Great Tongji Temple was versatile and capable;
he defeated Jiang Bin at the gates of the Wei court,
while Falin was a man of vast learning.
He eclipsed Fu Yi during the Tang Dynasty,
spread his magnificent virtue throughout his time,
and shook the world with his excellent reputation in these later ages.
However, as the distance from the sages has grown ever greater, demonic falsehoods have become indistinguishable from the truth;
purple and crimson are confused, and common stones are constantly mixed with jade.
Were it not for those of superior intelligence, who could possibly investigate and discern them?
Thus, the "rat-jade" falsely assumes its name;
the people of Zhou unified their standards for the noble and the base;
and the chicken and the phoenix differ in their forms.
The customs of Chu were confused regarding right and wrong;
consequently, there were those who clung to the literal letter of the texts and followed distorted interpretations,
rejecting [the truth] as the doctrine of a heterodox sect.
Though they employ clever words and deviant paths to draw others into discourse that accords with their own views,
it does not diminish the Ultimate Way by even a hair’s breadth.
Yet false doctrines claim that sensory objects exist for the eyes and ears;
this is why the dark path is so easy to fall upon,
and why the Gate of the Sages is so difficult to traverse.
When I originally came to possess the empire,
auspiciousness accorded with the Golden Wheel and portents coincided with the Jade Calendar;
I eclipsed the six directions and dwelt in glory over all lands.
It governs the myriad nations across its entire domain:
to the east it reaches the swirling peach trees, and to the west it extends to the slender willows;
to the south it shifts the golden cauldron, and to the north it reaches the jade balance.
Since the time of Lu Huxu, and following the eras of the Qin, Han, Sui, and Tang dynasties,
there has never been a period as flourishing as the present reign.
The Taizu and Taizong emperors issued clear edicts to provide protection and support.
Emperors Yuan and Ming renounced gold and jewels to cultivate and honor [the Dharma];
all shared in the thought of the mind of entrustment and together looked up to the teachings of compassion.
Exempting them from taxes and labor services to further develop their local customs and influence.
His Majesty the Emperor,
possessing profound benevolence and sagely wisdom, embodies the Way with broad-minded clarity.
He inherited the heroic foundation of the Four Sages and compiled the grand achievements of a hundred kings;
in the leisure of his myriad affairs, he looked with favor upon the Buddhist gate.
He recited the golden scriptures of the hundred thousand treasuries and convened an assembly of tens of thousands of monks;
he planted the seeds of merit in the Garden of Enlightenment and constructed a monastery.
His governance esteemed broad magnanimity and benevolence, such that its benefits reached the common people.
He sought out and promoted those from obscure and humble backgrounds, while demoting the unworthy and advancing the virtuous.
He clearly distinguished between the depths and shallows of the Buddhist and Daoist teachings.
He discerned the superiority and inferiority of the heterodox and the orthodox.
The Daoist, lacking any true insight,
held the state in contempt and deceived him with the promise of a residence in the north.
They indulge in the sophistry of their own private conjectures;
Qiu Chuji speaks falsely to flatter his superiors,
while Li Zhichang feigns refinement to curry favor with the times.
He gathered together the band of fugitive criminals who had evaded their duties and assembled the spurious scriptures that reject and subvert the [Buddhist] teachings;
Liu Hu-zhang was the first to compile these deluded doctrines.
Shizhi Jing further expanded upon heterodox texts,
imitating the eighty-two niches of the Tathāgata by compiling the eighty-one transformations of Laozi.
Failing to distinguish between the ancient and the modern, they lack mastery of both the Classics and the Histories;
they plunder and plagiarize Buddhist scriptures to incorporate them into Daoism,
and they borrow Buddhist portents to fabricate portents for Laozi.
He changed his surname to An and his name to Jiashang, altering "Jiashang" to "Laoxiang.
He arrogantly claimed these virtues as his own,
creating falsehood upon falsehood.
Building upon the void while suspended in the void:
Zhang Daoling and Li Er emerged from before the Great Vacuity;
Māluṅkyaputra and Kāśyapa descended during the era of King Zhuang of Zhou.
Establish biographies, images, and musical scores for circulation,
so that Yin Xi may become a Buddha and the aged Lao Dan may be honored as the ancestor of Śākyamuni.
Fuxi was granted instruction;
Gaoboyang served as the teacher of Fuxi and Nong;
the Sovereign of Xuanyuan sought the Way from Guangchengzi.
They maintain that Laozi was the teacher of King Wen,
and thus they deified him as the Lord Lao (Laojun).

The Duke of Zhou knelt before the bed of Laozi, who instructed him in the *Xuánjī jīng*; Confucius prostrated himself at the feet of his seat to inquire about the rites; thus, having eclipsed the three teachings, [Laozi] alone became manifest.
Transcending the thousand sages, he dwells in supreme honor;
solitary and lofty before the five dynasties,
he serves as the teacher beneath a hundred generations.
Within this realm, who else could be the sole Sage?
Though there are a hundred ways of clever adornment, not a single one possesses reality.
Examine this painting closely.
He desired to prune away the hundred schools to monopolize a single sect,
eclipsing the sagely achievements of Fuxi and Xuanyuan,
and extinguishing the grand principles of Śākyamuni and Confucius.
The world does not realize that these were the ultimate evils and great traitors.
Though there was the chaos of the state of Qiong during the Xia dynasty and the deception of Wang Mang toward the Han court, [the gravity of their crimes remains unrecognized].
This is not yet sufficient to surpass [the former].
Were it not for the Sovereign’s sagely wisdom and clear discernment free from delusion,
who else could investigate and distinguish between the true and the false, or perceive with their own eyes what is right and wrong?
Consequently, a special and luminous edict was issued to distinguish the false from the true;
thus, the malevolent root that had persisted for ten thousand years was uprooted all at once.
Thereupon, there appeared a master of the canonical teachings, the Abbot of Shaolin.
He was the pillar and foundation of the ancestral temple and the ridgepole and beam of the sacred halls;
his heart was upright and selfless,
and his nature was profound, clear, deep, and vast.
Compassionate toward their ignorance and blindness, he dispelled their delusions and prejudices;
he swept away the demonic miasma from the vast sky and raised high the radiant sun of the Buddha.
Xiangmai has heard this discourse from the side; it is impossible not to treasure these words.
I praise the divine intelligence of the Sage Ruler and admire the elegant responses from Shaolin.
I shall rely upon the authentic scriptures to refute and shatter these deluded discourses,
blocking the source of false teachings and overturning the forested thickets of the mountain of heterodoxy.
It caused the Great Lord of Jade to tremble with soul-shaking fear amidst the Nine Heavens;
it made the Primordial Celestial Honored One’s courage fail atop the Three Clarities;
and it left the Teacher of the Myriad Heavens shamed and unable to lift his head.
The immortals of the Nine Palaces were filled with such shame they had no place to hide.
I shall now list several items as examples to illustrate the rest,
so that the various qualities of gold and brass may be distinguished like the separate flows of the Jing and Wei rivers.
The jade nectar douses the entrails,
causing delusory cravings to dissipate;
the golden brush scrapes away the cataracts of ignorance.
It causes the eye of wisdom to become clear and distinct;
it serves as a nocturnal light for a dark chamber and as a morning mirror for a secluded path.
The man of universal enlightenment and penetration knows this Way.
In the second year of the Zhiyuan era, in the year of Zhánméng (the Wood Dragon), during the month of the Return of Yang in the Xiǎnjí mansion,
he brought his pen to rest at the Wànshòu Monastery.
1. Fabricated Claims Regarding the Heavenly Honored One, Part One. The first fabricated claim states:
"The Dao is the parent of the myriad transformations;
it is the ultimate and most honored of all that exists spontaneously."
Within this profound, mysterious, and subtle state, there arises the void;
the void is the True One (Zhenyi).
After the vital energy of the True One has undergone transformation and birth, it proceeds.
After ninety-nine trillion and ninety-nine million years had passed,
one is then born by transformation into the three upper realms of qi.
The distance between each of these three realms of qi is ninety-nine trillion and ninety-nine million years.
The three combined to form virtue, together giving birth to the Unsurpassed One,
who is the Supreme Sovereign Celestial Venerable (Xūhuáng Tiānzūn).
Furthermore, he passed through the aforementioned number of years.
Thereupon, the three middle qi were produced;
these three combined to form virtue, and thus Xuanlao was born—
this is none other than the Celestial Worthy of Original Commencement (Yuanshi Tianzun).
Furthermore, after passing through the aforementioned number of years,
the three lower vital energies (qi) were produced;
these three combined to form virtue, together giving birth to the Most High (Taishang).
This is none other than the Most High Lord of the Dao.
Thereafter, one *qi* (vital energy) again gave birth to three *qi*,
with each *qi* separated by eighty-one trillion and eighty-one million years.
The convergence of these three elements forms the virtue that gives birth to Lord Li (Laojun).
Although these four sages follow one another in succession, they do not depend upon one another;
this is termed "sole transformation" (duhua).
After the Old Lord was born, the five phases (wuyun) subsequently arose;
these are called Taiyi, Taichu, Taishi, Taisu, and Taiji.
The fifth transformation says:
The Lord of the Old is the progenitor of primordial chaos and the parents of heaven and earth; thus,
he was able to distribute the clear and the turbid, and open up and establish heaven and earth.
The commentator said:
"I have heard that there are the inscriptions of the Dragon Diagram and Bird Script,
and the records of the Tortoise Shell and Ko-ťou (Carpopogon) characters."
The records of the jade tablets and jade slips;
the books of the golden writs and golden caskets;
and the inscriptions of the Qin, Han, Wei, and Jin dynasties.
The annals and histories of the Song, Qi, Liang,
and Chen dynasties record events and history with direct penmanship and candid speech; therein,
the name of a "phantom Emperor" (Virtuous Sovereign) is nowhere to be seen.
If one has not heard the title of Yuanshi (Primordial Beginning),
how could there be one who holds a jade scepter in hand and wears yellow-brown robes upon the body?
With white hair hanging down from his crown,
he wears a golden tiara upon his head;
he is specially titled the Celestial Honored One (Tianzun).
Highly enshrined above the Three Purities,
he alone is titled the Master of Teachings;
he presides over the palace of the Nine Flowers.
Even if there is the title "Celestial Honored One" (Tianzun),
it is entirely a theft of the Buddha's words;
ancient scriptures referred to the Buddha by the name "Celestial Honored One."
This has no bearing on the affairs of the Celestial Venerable (Daojun).
To arrogantly assume his honorable title and falsely claim dignity in order to gain the trust of the learned is a mistaken statement.
According to the *Liezi* and the *Yi Gouming jue*,
it is said that before heaven and earth were produced, there was the Great Ease (*taiyi*) and the Great Beginning (*taichu*).
There is the Great Beginning (Taishi),
there is the Great Purity (Taisu),
and there is the Ultimate Pole (Taiji).
The commentators all say:
"The Great Ease (Taiyi) is that which has not yet manifested qi;
the Great Beginning (Taichu) is the inception of qi."
The Great Beginning (*Taishi*) is the beginning of form.
The Great Primal Matter (*Taisu*) is the beginning of substance.
The Great Ultimate (*Taiji*) is the state where substance and form are already complete, yet remain in a chaotic, undifferentiated condition.
After the Great Ultimate (Tàijí), the Two Polarities (Liǎngyí) were produced;
these are called Heaven and Earth.
Indeed, names arise from reality.
In truth, [the Way] arises from names.
Once both name and reality are established,
the Way can then be practiced.
Prior to the state of Taiyi, all was a profound void;
vast and obscure, it was fundamentally beyond sound and form.
How could one dare to speak of it in vain?
The nine breaths give rise to delusions, and the four persons arise from emptiness;
it is like knocking on empty space in search of an echo.
From falsehood arises further falsehood,
like chasing a shadow to find its tracks.
Do you not reflect on this?
Once its name is established, it must have a substance;
once its substance is established, it must have a clan and lineage.
Now tell me: from whom was the Primordial Origin of the Supreme Sovereign born?
What is the origin of this clan, and where does it reside?
If there is a genealogy, from which book does it derive?
If there is no source, then it is merely a hollow fabrication.
Furthermore, prior to the void, there were originally no years;
now to mark a number of years only serves to further reveal empty exaggeration.
Indeed, numerical reckoning originated with Fuxi.
Jiazi was proclaimed by the Yellow Emperor;
to take the present to record the past, how much inversion there is!
Furthermore, are the Three Honored Ones above possessed of form, or are they formless?
If it possesses form,
it does not exist beyond the Great Simplicity;
rather, it is born from its parents.
There must be [specification of] era, time, place, clan, and personal name.
As it was previously stated that "the three pneumas arise together through shared virtue," this would mean that pneuma gives rise to pneuma.
It is not different from qi;
how then could it have form or name?
If it were formless, [how could it exist]?
In the seventh section of the *Benwu mingwei* (Original Non-existence and Names and Ranks), it says:
"In the first year of the Shanghuang era, on the second day of the ninth month, the Lord Lao went out to travel in the West River.
There he encountered the Celestial Worthy of Original Commencement riding in a jade carriage of eightfold radiance, drawn by a dark dragon of nine colors."
A multitude of immortals followed as attendants, holding flowered banners in their hands;
lions and white cranes let out resonant cries and songs as they gathered together upon the banks of the West River.
He conferred upon Laojun the Cavern-Mystery Jade Talisman (Dongxuan yufu). Who was this person?
Whether seeking him in advancement or retreat, there is no definitive standard.
Thus we know that the "sea-date" is a hollow talk, existing in name only but lacking reality;
it is like carving ice or chiseling snow— a futile waste of literary effort,
for such things are not even collected among the mountains and seas.
That which is not recorded in the *Dahuang*—
how can the clever embellishments of the mediocre and ignorant be worthy of belief?
The Lord Lao was the Grand Scribe during the decline of the Zhou dynasty.
He falsely claimed to be the progenitor of Chaos;
he evaded the chaos of the Zhou dynasty by passing through the Pass of the Passes (Hanguan),
and falsely claimed to be the father and mother of Heaven and Earth.
Since your own words are already contradictory,
why do you attack one another like the arrow and the halberd?
To cover one's ears while stealing a bell— seeking to hide it only makes it more exposed.
The Chapter on Ethics states:
"I have three treasures;
treasure them and uphold them."
First is benevolence;
second is frugality;
third is not daring to take precedence over others in the world.
The Old Lord offered the wife and children of the Hu king to the Hu troops to engage them in battle;
how could there be any compassion in this?
Yet he rides the carriage of the Jade Balance and sits within the Golden Gate.
He wears robes of nine-colored *vilīra* silk and is shaded by a canopy of nine radiant light-emitting cranes;
how could there be anything frugal about this?
Born from the beginningless and arising without cause,
it precedes the myriad paths and serves as the progenitor of the primal qi.
Observing the state before chaos was divided and viewing the condition before clarity and turbidity were distinguished,
it serves as the teacher of emperors and kings and acts as the mother of heaven and earth.
How could there be anyone who does not dare to take the lead for the world?
Gao Xian, styled Zhongchang, of Liaoyang,
traveled to the White Crane Observatory in Dongjing.
Upon seeing an image of the Three Pure Ones,
he pointed to the one on the right and asked, "What image is this?"
The master of the monastery replied,
"This is an image of the Old Lord (Laojun).
He was a person of which generation?"
He replied, "It was during the reign of King Ding of Zhou.
Again pointing to the left, he asked,
"What image is this?"
The Master said,
"This is an image of the Lord of the Way (Daojun). He was a person of which era?"
The Master was flustered and had not yet replied when Xian pointed to the central image and said,
"For now, let us spare this Primordial Celestial Venerable."
Those who heard it spread it about as a joke.
Second, regarding the false establishment of the era name "Kalpa-Transport" (Jièyùn): the second and third transformations state as follows.
In the beginning, there was the qi of the Great Void.
This qi struck one another, coming and going and shooting in all directions.
After passing through hundreds of billions of cycles of qi, it reached its transformation.
Its qi is currently relaxed as it flows back and forth;

this is the natural qi, which refers to the event of the wind-wheel (vāyu-maṇḍala) swirling downward when the world was first formed. It is also called the qi of the ten thousand Brahmās of the Mahāmeru.
Furthermore, after ninety-nine thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine billion breaths,
he bound together the auspicious breaths to become one sage.
He styled himself the Celestial King of Primordial Beginning (Yuanshi Tianwang).
Simultaneously, he produced the Five Elders, the masters of the Five Elements;
that kalpa was named Yan'gang, and its era was named Longhan.
After another period of time as previously described,
the kalpa of the Dao-jun arose, named Chiming;
the year was likewise named Chiming.
Simultaneously, nine elders were born,
who divided themselves into the Nine Heavens;
they further underwent the same number of kalpas as mentioned above.
During the era when Laojun first appeared,
the kalpa was named Qingyun and the year was titled Shanghuang.
At that time, eight officials were produced.
Furthermore, the Five Phases (Wuyun)—Taiyi, Taichu, and so forth—were established.
The Lord Lao (Laojun) then combined the two qi of Yin and Yang to form the primordial chaos (hundun).
Thus, as they were distributed throughout heaven and earth, the myriad things first became complete.
Bian said:
"I have heard that in Ban Gu’s 'Treatise on Music and Calendrical Science' (Lüli zhi), it is stated:"
The *Tianguan* chapter of the *Shiji*,
the *Dinian* of Huangfu Mi,
and the *Diji* of Tao Hongjing.
Before the five phases of destiny were heard of, there were no era names;
within the three pneumas, the name "kalpa" was established in vain,
as neither clarity nor turbidity had yet taken form.
It is merely a vast, nebulous breath of qi.
How could there be Laojun, Yuanshi, the Five Elders, or the Nine Heavens?
Although they have pilfered the Buddhist term for "kalpa" (aeon) to establish their own system, [it remains fundamentally different].
Yet they do not understand the cycles of formation and destruction.
In Sanskrit this is called *kalpa*;
here it is translated as "time-period."
Although the durations of time differ, all are designated by the name *kalpa*.
This is a corruption of the Sanskrit term that confuses its essential nature and characteristics;
it is because the teachings of Śākyamuni have not yet reached this land.
It refers only to the act of robbing by means of violence; as Xu Shen’s *Shuowen Jiezi* states:
"To seize a person by force with weapons is called 'jie' (robbery).
Furthermore, the Lu general Cao Mo took the Marquis Huan hostage upon the altar and demanded back the territories that had been seized from him.
This refers to the act of seizing and plundering, which is what is meant by "kalpa" (劫);
how could there be any reference here to the concept of a cosmic eon?
That you now cite this term is a case of reckless and improper appropriation of my views.
Now that titles and positions have been established, the era designation is proclaimed;
this is intended to lead the myriad regions and bring order to the four seas,
unifying the nine provinces under a single system of chariots and books.
The Son of Heaven, being most honored, is entitled to establish a reign era;
those without name or rank dare not do so.
Although Confucius, despite having edited the *Shujing* and codified the rites to distinguish between ruler and subject, [did not establish such an era].
Since even one who holds no noble rank is merely titled the "Plain King" (Sùwáng),
how much more so for Lǎo Dān, who was a subordinate official— the Archivist of the Zhōu dynasty— among the ranks of ministers and sons!
How could he have dared to usurp the title of Emperor and recklessly establish a reign era?

Moreover, prior to Emperor Xuan there was originally no system of *jiǎzǐ* (sexagenary cycle); it was Huangdi’s minister Da Nao who created the *jiǎzǐ*. It was during the era of Emperor Wu that the practice of establishing reign titles (*niánhào*) first began; by instituting these titles, the Emperor sought to commemorate antiquity through antiquity itself.
How could this be false?
Some say that Laozi was born before heaven and earth.
What contradiction is there in establishing a separate era name?
The answer is:
Being already above heaven and earth,
it exists prior to the state of Great Simplicity (Tàiyì). At this time,
the world has not yet taken form.
There are no traces of sovereign or subject;
all is profoundly empty and still, a single vast expanse of mist.
Who establishes the era name and who exercises authority?
Though they clearly know this is a theft of the Buddha’s adornments and the intent of the Constellations of the Worthy Kalpa,
they nevertheless establish these labels of the "Yan-kang, Chi-ming, and Qing-yun" eras.
That [text] elucidates the three periods of time,
whereas this concerns a single moment;
it is exactly like the mountain tribesman who stole the king’s clothing and possessions.
Deluded and inverted, they have lost the proper order of high and low.
As it says below:
"Laozi was born on Tenggāng Lìgǔ; his courtesy name was Guāngmíng."
Thus, [the Laozi] must have been composed after the Three Sovereigns.
How could it be that the Old Lord (Laojun) took the two qi of yin and yang, joined them to form the Chaos (hundun), and distributed Heaven and Earth?
The forced interpretations at both the beginning and the end are clearly evident.
Section Three: The False Division of the Three Realms. The third and fifth transformation states:
"Heaven and earth are the greatest of all things possessing form.
The Most High Lord Lao (Taishang Laojun)..."
He is the progenitor of Chaos and the parent of Heaven and Earth; thus,
he was able to distribute the clear and the turbid, and open up and establish Heaven and Earth.
It was formed by the circulation of the three primordial qi of the Mysterious Origin (xuanyuan) and Beginning (shǐ).
In the heavens, these constitute the Three Purities (sānqīng) and the Three Realms (sānjìng);
specifically, the qi of Beginning constitutes the Realm of Jade Purity (Yùqīngjìng).
The primal qi constitutes the Realm of Supreme Purity (Shangqing);
the profound qi constitutes the Realm of Great Purity (Taiqing).
Furthermore, each of the qi of the Three Purities gives rise to three qi.
These combine the nine qi to form the Nine Heavens:
first, the Uttarakuru Heaven;
second, the Heaven of Immeasurable Life in the Upper Dhyāna.
The third is the Brahmāpariṣadya Heaven;
the fourth is the Yāma Heaven;
the fifth is the Tuṣita Heaven; and the sixth is the Nirmāṇarati Heaven.
The sixth is the Cavernous Mystery Heaven of Responding to Sounds;
the seventh is the Spiritually Transformed Heaven of Brahma’s Retinue;
the eighth is the High and Vast Heaven of Pure Clarity.
The ninth is the Heaven of Non-conceptualization and Non-craving.
These nine heavens each produce three vital energies (*prāṇa*),
and each energy constitutes one heaven.
These comprise twenty-seven heavens;
together with these nine heavens, they constitute thirty-six heavens.
Thus, from the Three Realms and the Four Classes of Beings up to the ultimate height of the Three Clarities (Sanqing).
This is their number.
First, the six heavens below constitute the realm of desire (kāmadhātu).
The first is the Great Yellow Heaven (Taihuáng tiān).
2. Tai-ming Heaven;
3. Qing-ming Heaven;
4. Xuan-tai Heaven.
The five [deities] are the Heaven of the Bright and Pure;
the six are the Heaven of the Seven Luminaries.
Next, the eighteen heavens constitute the Realm of Form (Rūpadhātu).
First, the Heaven of Emptiness and Non-being;
second, the Heaven of the Great Ultimate (Taiji);
third, the Heaven of Crimson Radiance.
Fourth is the Heaven of Adorned Flowers;
fifth is the Heaven of Luminous Stars;
sixth is the Heaven of Sovereign Music.
7. Lingming Heaven;
8. Duanjing Heaven;
9. Yuanming Heaven.
10. Jixi Yaotian;
11. Yuandai Tian; 12. Tai'an Tian.
13. The Heaven of Ultimate Wind;
14. The Heaven of Original Sovereign;
15. The Heaven of Great Yellow.
16. The Heaven of No-Thought (Avṛha);
17. The Heaven of Utmost Joy (Atapa);
18. The Heaven of Cloudless Radiance (Sudṛśa).
Next, the four heavens constitute the Formless Realm (ārūpyadhātu):
first, the Heaven of No-Strife (asaṃjñisattva);
second, the Heaven of Nothingness (ākiṃcanyāyatana).
Third, the Heaven of Sublime Accomplishment;
fourth, the Heaven of Transcendent Prohibition.
These twenty-eight heavens are called the Three Realms.
Above these are four other heavens called the Seed Human Heavens:
first, the Constantly Merged Heaven;
second, the Jadelong Heaven.
Third is the Heaven of the Brahma-Prakāśa;
fourth is the Heaven of Akaniṣṭha.
These four heavens transcend the three realms.
It is further stated:
"The three heavens above constitute the realm of the Three Clarities (*Trisvabhāva*).
